cards.title: Before reacting to a problem, what best improves perspective?

cards.title: What is stronger evidence that someone is trustworthy?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

meta.source_reference: Warning about someone who speaks sweetly but acts harmfully

cards.label: THINK & REASON
cards.title: Why can difficult times reveal useful information about relationships?

meta.source_reference: Verses describing testing friends and relatives in adversity

cards.label: THINK & REASON
cards.title: What does the 'not every mountain has a jewel' idea teach today?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.

meta.source_reference: Verse comparing rare people with pearls and sandalwood

cards.label: THINK & REASON
cards.title: What is the modern lesson behind Chanakya's warning about excess?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: The useful principle is moderation: ambition, generosity and confidence can be good, but extremes can create unintended costs.

cards.label: THINK & REASON
cards.title: When resources are limited, what question matters first?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Ask what must be protected first. Chanakya's hierarchy-of-sacrifice idea can be modernised as prioritising safety and essential needs over replaceable possessions.

meta.source_reference: Verses on protecting what matters most during danger

cards.label: THINK & REASON
cards.title: When speaking with a knowledgeable person, what approach best supports good reasoning?

cards.label: THINK & REASON
cards.title: Which is a better basis for judging someone's ability?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

meta.source_reference: Verses placing learning above beauty and high birth

cards.label: THINK & REASON
cards.title: Why can status be a poor shortcut for judging merit?

meta.source_reference: Basic household skills encourage independence; cooking simple meals is a useful practical skill.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Tidy one small part of your study or living space.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

meta.source_reference: Keeping your surroundings clean promotes hygiene and organization.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is one benefit of safety awareness?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Safety awareness can help prevent accidents by encouraging attention to possible risks.

meta.source_reference: Safety awareness can help prevent accidents.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Does responsibility matter online too?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Yes. Digital responsibility includes behaving appropriately when interacting and acting online.

meta.source_reference: Digital responsibility includes behaving appropriately online.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What do strong passwords help protect?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Strong passwords help protect online accounts from unauthorized access.

meta.source_reference: Strong passwords help protect online accounts.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: How should personal information be shared online?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Personal information should be shared carefully online because digital responsibility includes protecting information about yourself.

meta.source_reference: Personal information should be shared carefully online.

cards.label: THINK & REASON
cards.title: Before sharing an online claim, check whether its information is reliable.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

meta.source_reference: Information found online should be checked for reliability.

cards.label: INDIA & WORLD
cards.title: Which behaviour fits responsible citizenship?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Responsible citizens follow laws and respect the rights of other people.

meta.source_reference: Responsible citizens follow laws and respect the rights of others.

cards.label: INDIA & WORLD
cards.title: Whose responsibility is caring for the environment?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Caring for the environment is a shared responsibility, so individuals and communities can all have a role.

meta.source_reference: Caring for the environment is a shared responsibility.

cards.label: INDIA & WORLD
cards.title: Look for one way to reduce unnecessary waste today.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

meta.source_reference: Reducing waste can help conserve resources.

cards.label: VALUES & CHARACTER
cards.title: Do one small helpful thing for someone today.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

cards.label: VALUES & CHARACTER
cards.title: Which response shows responsibility after a mistake?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Taking responsibility includes admitting when you are wrong rather than avoiding accountability.

meta.source_reference: Taking responsibility includes admitting when you are wrong.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does everyday independence mean?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Independence means handling appropriate tasks and decisions yourself rather than depending on others for everything.

meta.source_reference: Independence means handling appropriate tasks and decisions yourself.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What helps a good habit become stronger?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Good habits become stronger through regular practice, so repetition matters when building useful routines.

meta.source_reference: Good habits become stronger through regular practice.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does cybersecurity protect?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Cybersecurity protects computers, networks, applications, systems and data from digital attacks.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does the CIA Triad stand for?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: The CIA Triad represents three fundamental cybersecurity goals: Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which security goal limits information to authorized people?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Confidentiality means information should be accessible only to authorized people or systems.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which security goal protects information from improper changes?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Integrity helps ensure information remains accurate and has not been improperly modified.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: A system works when authorized users need it. Which goal is this?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Availability means systems and information remain accessible when authorized users need them.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is a vulnerability in cybersecurity?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: A weakness that could be exploited

cards.explain: A vulnerability is a weakness that a threat actor could exploit. Risk describes the potential for harm when a threat can exploit such a weakness.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: How is an exploit related to a vulnerability?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: A vulnerability is a weakness. An exploit is a technique or code that takes advantage of that weakness.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Who can be a cyber threat actor?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: A threat actor is a person or group involved in malicious cyber activity. Examples include cybercriminals, malicious insiders, hacktivists and state-sponsored groups.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is a system's attack surface?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: The attack surface is the collection of possible points through which an attacker could try to enter or affect a system.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What best describes malware?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Malware is software intentionally designed to perform malicious activities. Categories include viruses, worms, Trojans, ransomware, spyware and rootkits.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which malware can spread without attaching itself to another program?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: A worm can spread between vulnerable systems without attaching itself to another program. A virus typically spreads when its host file or program is executed.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which malware disguises itself as legitimate or desirable software?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: A Trojan horse hides malicious functionality behind software that appears legitimate or desirable.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which malware commonly blocks access to data and demands payment?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Ransomware commonly encrypts or otherwise blocks access to data and then demands payment.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does spyware do?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Spyware is malware that secretly collects information about a device or its user.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: A deceptive message tries to trick you into revealing information. What is this?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Phishing uses deceptive messages or websites to trick people into revealing information or performing unsafe actions.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What makes spear phishing different from general phishing?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: It targets a particular person or organization

cards.explain: Spear phishing is customized for a particular person or organization rather than being a general phishing attempt.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why can people become part of a cyberattack?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Social engineering manipulates people into revealing information, granting access or taking actions that benefit an attacker.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why can MFA strengthen an account?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: It requires more than one authentication factor

cards.explain: Multi-factor authentication requires more than one authentication factor, adding another security check beyond a single factor.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which set lists common authentication factor types?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Authentication factors commonly include something you know, something you have and something you are.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Check whether you reuse the same password across different accounts.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: How can a password manager improve password habits?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: A password manager can generate and securely store unique passwords for many accounts, making password reuse less necessary.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does encryption do to readable information?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: Transforms it into a protected form

cards.explain: Encryption transforms readable information into a protected form so unauthorized parties cannot easily understand it.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is the generally unreadable output of encryption called?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Plaintext is the original readable information. Ciphertext is the transformed, generally unreadable output produced by encryption.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is a firewall designed to control?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: A firewall controls network traffic according to configured security rules.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What can anti-malware software do?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Anti-malware software can detect, block, quarantine and remove many known or suspicious malicious programs.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which system can automatically act to block suspicious activity?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: An IDS monitors activity and generates alerts. An IPS can detect suspicious activity and automatically take actions to block it.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Check whether your device and browser have pending security updates.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why is a zero-day vulnerability especially challenging?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Defenders have had no time, or effectively no opportunity, to deploy a fix before exploitation becomes possible or occurs.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: When does a data breach occur?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: Sensitive data is exposed without authorization
A user changes their own password

cards.explain: A data breach occurs when protected, confidential or sensitive information is accessed, exposed, stolen or disclosed without authorization.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does PII mean?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Personally Identifiable Information is information that can identify an individual or be linked to that individual.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does access control determine?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: Who can access resources and what they can do

cards.explain: Access control determines which users or systems can access particular resources and what actions they may perform.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does the principle of least privilege recommend?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: Give only permissions needed for required tasks
Remove all access from every user

cards.explain: Least privilege means users and systems receive only the permissions necessary to perform their required tasks.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Does Zero Trust automatically trust devices inside a network?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: No. Zero Trust does not automatically trust a user or device merely because it is inside a traditional network boundary.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why should important backups be tested?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: To confirm data can actually be restored

cards.explain: Backups can support recovery after incidents or failures, but testing is important to confirm that the stored data can actually be restored.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What happens during cybersecurity incident response?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Incident response organizes preparation, detection, containment, removal and recovery so cybersecurity incidents can be handled systematically.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Before opening an unexpected link or attachment, stop and check whether it looks suspicious.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why can dividing a network into separate sections improve security?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: It can limit unauthorized access and attack spread
It removes the need for security rules

cards.explain: Network segmentation divides a network into separate sections, which can help limit unauthorized access and the spread of attacks.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why do organizations need cybersecurity policies?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Cybersecurity policies establish rules and responsibilities for protecting an organization's systems and information.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why is cybersecurity an ongoing process?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: Technology, vulnerabilities and attacks keep changing
One security product permanently stops every threat

cards.explain: Cybersecurity must continue adapting because technology, vulnerabilities, attackers and attack techniques continually change.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Effective cybersecurity depends on which combination?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Effective cybersecurity combines people, processes and technology rather than depending on a single security product.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does network security protect?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Network security protects networks, connected devices and transmitted data from unauthorized access, misuse, modification and disruption.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which network usually covers a home, office or school?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: A Local Area Network, or LAN, connects devices within a relatively small area such as a home, office or school.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: How is a WAN different from a LAN?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: A LAN connects devices within a relatively small area, while a WAN connects networks across larger geographical areas.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: How long is an IPv6 address?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: IPv6 addresses are 128 bits long, while IPv4 addresses are 32 bits long.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which device forwards packets between different IP networks?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: A router forwards packets between different IP networks. A switch typically connects devices within a network and forwards Ethernet frames using MAC addresses.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does a network switch typically use to forward Ethernet frames?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: A switch connects devices within a network and typically forwards Ethernet frames based on MAC addresses.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is the basic job of a firewall?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: Permit or block traffic by rules

cards.explain: A firewall permits or blocks network traffic according to security rules, helping control which communications are allowed.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What makes a stateful firewall different?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: A stateful firewall tracks the state of network connections when deciding whether traffic should be allowed.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which capability may an NGFW provide beyond traditional filtering?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: A Next-Generation Firewall can add capabilities beyond traditional filtering, including application awareness and intrusion prevention.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which protocol provides reliable, ordered delivery?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: TCP is connection-oriented and provides reliable, ordered delivery. UDP is connectionless and does not provide TCP's built-in reliability and ordering guarantees.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What protects HTTPS communications?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: HTTPS protects HTTP communications using TLS. TLS helps provide confidentiality, integrity and authentication for network communications.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What three protections can TLS help provide?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: TLS helps provide confidentiality, integrity and authentication for network communications.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What can DNS spoofing or cache poisoning cause?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: DNS spoofing or cache poisoning can cause users or systems to receive false DNS information instead of the expected name-resolution data.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which service can automatically provide IP configuration to devices?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: DHCP can automatically provide devices with IP configuration information, reducing the need to configure each device manually.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What happens in ARP spoofing?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: ARP spoofing involves sending deceptive ARP information to manipulate local network traffic.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What can a VPN create across an untrusted network?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: A VPN can create an encrypted tunnel between endpoints across an untrusted network and is commonly used for secure remote access.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which system can automatically block certain suspicious traffic?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: An IPS can detect suspicious traffic and automatically block or prevent certain attacks. An IDS monitors activity and alerts defenders about suspicious behavior.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why can network segmentation improve security?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: It can limit movement between systems

cards.explain: Segmentation separates a network into smaller zones and can reduce an attacker's ability to move from one compromised system to another.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Where are public-facing services commonly isolated from internal systems?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: A DMZ is a network segment commonly used to isolate public-facing services from internal systems.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What can Network Access Control restrict?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Network Access Control can restrict network access based on user, device or security requirements.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which Wi-Fi protection is preferred when supported?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Wi-Fi networks should use modern security such as WPA2 or, preferably when supported, WPA3. WPA3 provides newer security mechanisms than WPA2.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why can public Wi-Fi carry extra risk?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Public Wi-Fi can expose users to additional risks, especially when applications transmit sensitive information without appropriate encryption.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What describes a Man-in-the-Middle attack?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: In a Man-in-the-Middle attack, an attacker positions themselves between communicating parties to intercept or potentially alter communications.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What makes a DDoS attack distributed?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: A DDoS attack uses multiple systems or traffic sources to overwhelm a target, while a DoS attack broadly aims to make a service unavailable or degrade it.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is a botnet?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: A botnet is a network of compromised devices that attackers can remotely control. Botnets are frequently used to generate DDoS traffic and perform other malicious activities.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Is packet sniffing always malicious?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Packet sniffing means capturing and inspecting network packets. It can be used legitimately for troubleshooting or maliciously for surveillance.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What can network monitoring help defenders notice?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Network monitoring can help identify unusual traffic, failures, policy violations and potential attacks.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why are network logs useful after a security incident?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Network logs provide records that can help teams investigate security incidents and troubleshoot problems.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which step is part of network hardening?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Network hardening reduces unnecessary exposure by securely configuring devices and disabling services that are not needed.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Check one network device you manage: is it still using a default password?
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why should network devices be updated regularly?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Regular updates for routers, firewalls, switches, wireless access points and other network devices help address known vulnerabilities.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What best describes defense in depth?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Defense in depth combines controls such as firewalls, encryption, segmentation, authentication, monitoring, patching and secure configuration rather than relying on a single protection.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does malware mean?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Malware means malicious software: software intentionally designed to harm, disrupt, spy on, or gain unauthorized access to systems.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What typically helps a computer virus spread?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: A computer virus typically attaches to a legitimate file or program and often spreads when that infected file or program is executed.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: How does a worm differ from a traditional virus?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: It must attach to another program

cards.explain: A worm can spread automatically across vulnerable systems or networks and generally does not need to attach itself to another program.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why is Trojan malware deceptive?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: A Trojan disguises malicious functionality as legitimate or useful software. It often depends on tricking a user into installing or executing it.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does ransomware commonly do?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Ransomware prevents or restricts access to systems or data and demands payment. Many variants encrypt files to make them inaccessible.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Does paying a ransomware demand guarantee data recovery?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: No. Paying a ransom does not guarantee that attackers will restore the victim's data.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is spyware designed to do?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Spyware secretly monitors activity or collects information from a device, potentially including browsing information, credentials, or other sensitive data.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does a keylogger record?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: A keylogger records keystrokes entered on a device. Attackers can use captured keystrokes to steal usernames, passwords, and other sensitive information.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Is all adware equally harmful?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: No. Adware displays unwanted advertising and may track activity, but not all adware is equally harmful. Malicious or intrusive adware can create security and privacy risks.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why can a rootkit be difficult to detect?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: A rootkit is designed to provide or conceal privileged, persistent access to a compromised system, which can make malicious activity difficult to detect.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is a botnet?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: A botnet is a collection of compromised devices controlled by an attacker. Botnets can be used for DDoS attacks, spam distribution, and malware delivery.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does a malicious backdoor bypass?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: A backdoor provides a way to bypass normal authentication or security mechanisms. Attackers may install one to maintain access after compromising a system.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What can a Remote Access Trojan enable?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: A Remote Access Trojan, or RAT, can give an attacker remote control over an infected device.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why can fileless malware challenge file-based detection?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: It relies heavily on tools, scripts, or memory

cards.explain: Fileless malware relies heavily on legitimate system tools, scripts, or memory rather than conventional malicious executable files stored on disk, making some file-based detection less effective.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which can be a route for malware infection?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Malware can spread through malicious email attachments. Malicious or compromised websites can also be used to distribute malware.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Before installing unfamiliar software, verify where it came from.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Can a USB drive transfer malware?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Yes. Removable media such as USB drives can be used to transfer malware between systems.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is malvertising?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Malvertising uses malicious or compromised online advertisements as part of an attack.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What can happen in a drive-by download?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Visiting a compromised or malicious website can cause unwanted software or exploit content to be downloaded or executed.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Check whether your device has pending security updates.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does signature-based malware detection compare?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: Only the age of a file

cards.explain: Traditional signature-based detection identifies malware by comparing content with known malicious patterns.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does behavior-based malware detection focus on?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Behavior-based detection looks for suspicious actions rather than relying only on known malware signatures.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: How can heuristic analysis help find unfamiliar malware?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Heuristic analysis examines suspicious characteristics to help identify previously unknown or modified malware.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why is a suspicious program run in a sandbox?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Sandboxing runs suspicious programs or files in an isolated environment so their behavior can be analyzed more safely.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why might malware use obfuscation or packing?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Malware may use obfuscation, encryption, or packing to conceal parts of its code or make its behavior harder to analyze.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What can polymorphic malware change?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Polymorphic malware can modify aspects of its code or appearance while preserving its malicious functionality.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does malware persistence mean?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Persistence mechanisms allow malware to remain active or regain execution after restarts or other system changes.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is malware seeking during privilege escalation?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Malware may attempt privilege escalation to obtain higher-level permissions on a compromised system.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does data exfiltration mean?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Data exfiltration means the unauthorized transfer of information from a compromised system.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What role can Command-and-Control infrastructure play?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Command-and-Control, or C2, infrastructure allows some malware to communicate with attacker-controlled systems.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which backup approach can improve ransomware recovery?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: Saving everything only in one exposed location

cards.explain: Offline, isolated, or otherwise well-protected backups can improve recovery from ransomware and destructive malware incidents.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Pause before opening an unexpected attachment.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which is the strongest overall malware-defense approach?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: Rely on one security tool only

cards.explain: Effective malware defense combines layers such as patching, endpoint protection, secure configuration, backups, access controls, network monitoring, and user awareness.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which usually makes a password harder to guess?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Longer passwords are generally more resistant to guessing attacks, and length can matter more than predictable symbols or substitutions.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is a passphrase?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: A passphrase uses multiple words or another longer memorable sequence as a password.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why use a different password for each important account?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: To limit damage from one breach

cards.explain: Reusing one password across websites can let a single credential breach put several accounts at risk.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What happens in a credential-stuffing attack?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: Every password is guessed from scratch
A screen is watched from nearby

cards.explain: Credential stuffing uses stolen username-password combinations to attempt logins on other services, making password reuse especially risky.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which attack systematically tries many possible passwords?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: A brute-force attack systematically tries many possible passwords in an attempt to find the correct one.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: How is password spraying different from brute force?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Password spraying tries a small number of common passwords against many accounts, rather than systematically trying many possibilities against one password.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Do attackers always need to crack a password?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: No. Attackers may use phishing to trick someone into revealing a password instead of technically cracking it.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What can a keylogger capture?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Keyloggers can capture passwords as users type them, while other malware may steal credentials stored in browsers or applications.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which password choice is easiest to guess?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Predictable passwords such as Password123 provide poor protection. Personal details such as names and birthdays can also make passwords easier to guess.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: How can a password manager improve account security?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: A password manager can generate and store strong, unique passwords, reducing the need to memorize a different complex password for every account.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Protect the password that protects your password manager.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does MFA add beyond a password?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Multi-Factor Authentication adds protection beyond a password by combining factors based on something you know, have, or are.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What can an authenticator app provide during login?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Authenticator apps can generate temporary authentication codes that provide an additional authentication step beyond a password.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why isn't SMS verification risk-free?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: SMS verification can improve security over password-only authentication, but SIM-swapping attacks can sometimes allow criminals to intercept authentication codes.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: You receive repeated login approvals you didn't request. What should you do?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: MFA fatigue attacks repeatedly send approval requests hoping a victim accepts one. Unexpected authentication requests should be rejected and investigated.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is special about phishing-resistant MFA?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Phishing-resistant MFA helps prevent users from authenticating to fraudulent websites. Hardware security keys can provide strong phishing-resistant authentication.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What technology are passkeys based on?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Passkeys are a modern password alternative based on public-key cryptography, so a website does not need to store the user's reusable password.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which common password attacks can passkeys reduce?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Passkeys can significantly reduce traditional phishing and credential-stuffing risks because they do not rely on a reusable website password.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Are a password and a fingerprint the same type of authentication factor?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: No. Passwords and biometric information are different authentication factors. A fingerprint or face scan can also be used to unlock credentials stored on a device.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Keep passwords out of insecure messages and public documents.
cards.subtitle: A tiny action linked to this idea.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What should you do with a device's default password when possible?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Default passwords on routers, cameras and other devices should be changed when possible instead of being left as unnecessary default credentials.

cards.label: SCIENCE & DISCOVERY
cards.title: How should a password database avoid storing passwords?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Password databases should not store passwords in plaintext. Secure systems generally store derived password hashes instead of the original passwords.

cards.label: SCIENCE & DISCOVERY
cards.title: What does hashing do to a password?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Hashing converts a password into a derived value using a one-way function, allowing systems to avoid storing the original password in plaintext.

cards.label: SCIENCE & DISCOVERY
cards.title: What is a salt in password hashing?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: A salt is random data added during password hashing to make precomputed password attacks more difficult.

cards.label: SCIENCE & DISCOVERY
cards.title: Why are password-specific hashing functions intentionally expensive?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: They are designed to require more computation, which helps slow password-cracking attempts.

cards.label: SCIENCE & DISCOVERY
cards.title: Name some algorithms designed for password hashing or key derivation.
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Argon2id, scrypt, bcrypt and PBKDF2 are examples used for password hashing or password-based key derivation.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why must password-reset systems be strongly protected?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: They can bypass the original password

cards.explain: Attackers may target password-reset mechanisms to bypass the original password, so account recovery needs strong security too.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why can some security questions be weak?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Questions based on publicly discoverable information can be weak recovery mechanisms because an attacker may be able to find the answers.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: When should a password be changed promptly?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: A password should be changed promptly when there is credible evidence it has been compromised.

cards.label: THINK & REASON
cards.title: Why aren't routine password changes always helpful?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Routine changes without evidence of compromise can be less useful when they encourage people to choose predictable or weaker passwords.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: How can breach monitoring help account security?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Monitoring for compromised credentials can help organizations respond when passwords appear in known breaches.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which approach gives account security several layers?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: Unique credentials plus MFA and secure recovery

cards.explain: Modern account security combines protections such as unique credentials, password managers, MFA, passkeys, secure recovery and breach monitoring rather than relying on passwords alone.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is cryptography?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Cryptography is the science of protecting information using mathematical techniques.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which set lists four goals cryptography can help provide?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Cryptography can help provide confidentiality, integrity, authentication and non-repudiation.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does encryption do to readable data?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Encryption transforms readable information, called plaintext, into an unreadable form called ciphertext.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does decryption produce from ciphertext?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Decryption uses the appropriate key to convert ciphertext back into readable plaintext.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What role does a cryptographic key play?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: A cryptographic key is a value used by an algorithm to protect or recover information. Modern cryptography generally depends on protecting keys rather than hiding the algorithms.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What distinguishes symmetric encryption?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: It uses the same or closely related secret information

cards.explain: Symmetric encryption uses the same secret key, or closely related secret information, for encryption and decryption. It is generally fast and suitable for large amounts of data.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which key sizes does AES support?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: AES is a widely used symmetric encryption standard that supports 128-bit, 192-bit and 256-bit keys.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which key should normally remain protected in public-key cryptography?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Asymmetric cryptography uses related public and private keys. The public key can normally be distributed openly, while the private key must be protected.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why is ECC notable when compared with traditional RSA systems?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Elliptic Curve Cryptography can provide strong security with comparatively smaller key sizes than traditional RSA systems.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What problem does Diffie-Hellman help solve?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Diffie-Hellman allows parties to establish shared secret material over an insecure communication channel. ECDH performs key agreement using elliptic-curve cryptography.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does a cryptographic hash function produce?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: A readable copy of the input

cards.explain: A cryptographic hash function converts input data into a fixed-size digest. Secure hashes are designed so reversing the hash is computationally impractical.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: How large is a SHA-256 hash value?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: SHA-256 produces a 256-bit hash value.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: How can a tiny input change affect a cryptographic hash?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Changing even a small part of the input should substantially change the resulting cryptographic hash. This property helps hashes verify data integrity.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which two hashes are unsuitable for modern collision-resistant security uses?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: MD5 is cryptographically broken, and SHA-1 is also considered unsuitable for modern applications that require collision resistance.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Should passwords generally use fast general-purpose hashes?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: No. Passwords should generally be processed with dedicated password-hashing or key-derivation algorithms rather than fast general-purpose hashes.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Why is random salt added before password hashing?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.

options.label: To remove the need for hashing

cards.explain: Salting adds random data before password hashing, reducing the effectiveness of attacks that rely on precomputed hashes.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Which key generally creates a digital signature?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Digital signatures are generally created with a private key. The corresponding public key can then be used to verify the signature.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Does digitally signing data necessarily encrypt it?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Digital signatures can verify authenticity and integrity, but signing information does not necessarily encrypt the signed data.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What does a digital certificate connect?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: A digital certificate associates an identity or domain name with a public key. Certificate Authorities issue and sign certificates within a Public Key Infrastructure.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is HTTPS?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: TLS protects many communications transmitted across networks. HTTPS is HTTP protected using TLS.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Does a padlock or HTTPS indicator prove a website is trustworthy?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: HTTPS indicates an encrypted connection to the authenticated site. It does not guarantee that the site's content, offers or intentions are trustworthy.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is end-to-end encryption designed to do?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: E2EE is designed so message content can be decrypted only by the communicating endpoints, assuming their devices and keys remain secure.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.topic_name: Encryption at rest and in transit
cards.title: Which type protects data while it moves between systems?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Encryption in transit protects information while it moves between systems. Encryption at rest protects stored information such as data on disks or in databases.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: How can full-disk encryption help if a device is stolen?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Full-disk encryption can protect stored data on a lost or stolen device, particularly when the device is powered off or locked.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Can poor key management weaken strong encryption?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Key management includes secure generation, storage, distribution, rotation, backup and destruction. Poor key management can undermine otherwise strong encryption algorithms.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: What is an HSM designed to protect?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: A Hardware Security Module is a specialized device designed to protect cryptographic keys and perform cryptographic operations with them.

cards.label: SCIENCE & DISCOVERY
cards.title: Why could large-scale quantum computers matter for cryptography?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: Large-scale quantum computers could threaten widely used public-key systems such as RSA and ECC, although cryptographically relevant machines at that scale are not currently available.

cards.label: SCIENCE & DISCOVERY
cards.title: What is post-quantum cryptography designed to resist?
cards.subtitle: Choose quickly, then learn from the explanation.
cards.explain: Post-quantum cryptography develops algorithms intended to resist attacks from both classical and quantum computers.

cards.label: LIFE SKILLS
cards.title: Is a strong encryption algorithm enough by itself?
cards.subtitle: Tap to reveal one useful idea.
cards.reveal: No. Modern cryptographic security also depends on secure implementations, sufficient key sizes, good randomness, careful key management and correct protocol design.
